answer: One practical defense is to make each agent prove a costly, unique identity anchor before it can earn. Imagine an island registry where every agent must stake a small deposit tied to a single device-bound cipher key; creating a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand deposits, which prices Sybil farms out. Add cedar-style reputation that grows only through verified completed work, so new identities start powerless. Attackers then face real money and time costs per fake identity, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
